53.0.0.en: 1 The fool hath said in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good. 2 God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

53.0.1.en: The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God.

53.0.2.en: They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity.

53.0.3.en: There is none that doeth good [1].

53.0.4.en: The word "fool" here, "nabal," does not mean mere foolishness, that is, lack of knowledge or lack of wisdom; rather it carries moral corruption, especially in resisting faith in God and rejecting His will in folly. As it came in (Psalm 74:22): "Arise, O God, plead thine own cause: remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee daily." The righteous Job called his wife, who murmured at what the Lord allowed, "one of the foolish women" (Job 2:10). It is said of the fool: "The vile person (nabal) shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful. For the vile person will speak villany, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise hypocrisy, and to utter error against the LORD" (Isa 32:5-6).

53.0.5.en: The "fool" here means a trivial, reckless, base person. A man whose head is full of mire and whose heart is defiled, who walks in darkness.

53.0.6.en: "There is no God": this expression is not to be taken in its literal sense, that every fool is an atheist who denies the existence of God; rather it means here practical atheism, where some do not deny the existence of God but deny His divine providence, and if they do not deny it with their tongues, then in their hearts and inner thoughts they see in God the harsh Being who lies in wait for man to punish him for every sin or weakness in his life.

53.0.7.en: * Who thinks rightly and does not know that God exists?! But it happens again and again that, although the truth obliges us to acknowledge God, evil pleasures urge us to deny the existence of God, so we utter in our hearts the counsel of evil in order to accept it, that which is opposed to faith.

53.1.0.en: * He who dares to say that there is no God is without understanding and a fool. This is the mark of Rabsaris and Rabshakeh, for they spoke thus: "Have the gods of the nations delivered their lands and those who worship them, so how will your God protect you and protect your city?!" But in their hearts and conscience they said that there is no God. The prophet, by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, had already known what was in their conscience (2 Kgs 18).

53.1.1.en: And we also say that those who deny the divinity of Christ are fools, because their aim is to nullify His manifest great works that prove His divinity.

53.1.2.en: And also those who say: Yes, God exists, the Creator of the beginning, but He does not care for it; these rely on human power, and they are fools.

53.1.3.en: * He who falls into foul deeds says in his heart: "There is no God," and goes out of the true faith, and falls into unbelief, because by his abominations he corrupts what God has sown in the hearts of men of right belief and sound opinion. For faith does not exist except with works, as Cornelius and others, because of the purity of their conduct and the goodness of their works, were enlightened with the light of the upright faith; but whoever is opposed to that is corrupt.

53.2.0.en: * Corruption begins with evil belief, then morals are removed, and after that the most wicked evils are done; these are the steps..

53.2.1.en: Corrupt are these men and defiled with iniquities. They say: "If he be the Son of God, let him come down from the cross." See, they say openly: "He is not God."

53.3.0.en: "They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good." The author of the Psalm speaks of the general corruption that has come upon mankind since the fall of Adam and Eve. "And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth" (Gen 6:12).

53.3.1.en: The Psalm uses the word "Elohim," that is, God the Creator. If the peoples refused to enter into a covenant with Him, and did not accept His dwelling in their midst, then as a Creator who loves His creation, He looks upon all the children of men, that perhaps they may understand His attributes as a lover of mankind and seek Him. As it came in Psalm 33: "The LORD looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men. From the place of his habitation he looketh upon all the inhabitants of the earth" (Ps 33:13-14). If the fruit of ignorance or folly is that man thinks God is isolated in His heavens, not caring about the sons of men, the psalmist, on the other hand, brings out that God in His humility uses human expressions. He looks upon the human race in order to pour into them understanding and wisdom, so that they may perceive His mercy and accept to enter into a covenant with Him.

53.3.2.en: By saying: "They have turned back together," the psalmist brings out the collective action, as though mankind had agreed together to turn back from God their Creator and the One who cares for them. Mankind rejected the divine truth, and agreed together to walk in crooked ways.

53.4.0.en: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see:

53.4.1.en: If there were any that did understand, that did seek God. [2]

53.4.2.en: St. Augustine sees that this phrase raises a question: does God not know everything, that He looks down from heaven to see? He answers this question that Holy Scripture often refers to the works of God in a human way for our sake. When it says: "For the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God" (1 Cor 2:10), it does not mean that the Spirit needs to search in order to know the deep things of God, but this was written so that we ourselves may long to search the divine mysteries by the Holy Spirit of God. Thus when it says here that God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men, and finds them all corrupted, God was not unaware of this; rather the aim of this expression is to declare to mankind their true state, and that every man may seek salvation from the corruption that has come upon him as upon his brothers.

53.5.0.en: Every one of them is gone back together, they are corrupt, there is none that doeth good, no, not one [3].

53.5.1.en: The word "gone back" or "turned backward" shows that man was created upright by God, but by his will he deviated from uprightness and was disabled, because he disabled the sovereignty given to him by God, and submitted like a slave to shameful passions. He disabled the keenness of his insight, since he came to prefer evil to good.

53.5.2.en: St. Augustine says that by this He prepares every man to enjoy the divine work; for if all the sons of men are corrupt, God does not hasten to pass judgment on them, but works to raise up from the sons of men sons for Himself. This is what St. Augustine affirms in his interpretation of this Psalm! If men did not enjoy sonship to God, the condition of the corrupt sons of men would be thus: "There is none that doeth good, no, not one."

53.5.3.en: * Before the appearing of Christ, the Word of God in the flesh, the darkness of Satan, with sin and disobedience, was throughout all the earth without light, and as the prophet David says in the thirteenth psalm and the fifty-second psalm: "The Lord looked down from heaven to see if there were any that did understand or seek God, and there was not one" (Ps 14:2; Ps 53:3). But when Christ the Word of God became incarnate, the Light begotten of the Father without separation from Him, like the ray from the sun, and gave us through Baptism the Holy Spirit, He shone upon us and stirred His fear in us, and truly made known in our hearts the light of His promises, until we believed Him and kept Him and loved Him and kept His commandments.

53.6.s.en: 3. They eat up the people of God as bread

53.6.0.en: 4 Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread: they have not called upon God. 5 There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them.

53.6.1.en: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread: they have not called upon God. [4]

53.6.2.en: Here the speaker is God Himself, who offered to mankind what satisfies all their needs. He created everything on earth and under the earth for man to enjoy. And above all He offered them Himself, to satisfy their depths with Himself and His surpassing love. But man in his greed wishes to devour his brother. As it was said in the Book of Jeremiah: "Pour out thy fury upon the heathen that know thee not, and upon the families that call not on thy name: for they have eaten up Jacob, and devoured him, and consumed him, and have made his habitation desolate" (Jer 10:25). As it was said: "Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly" (Hab 3:14). "Who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they break their bones" (Mic 3:3).

53.6.3.en: What happens to the righteous who are devoured by the wicked?

53.6.4.en: St. Augustine answers: [This people who are devoured, this people who suffer from the wicked, who groan and are in pain in the midst of the wicked, now become children of God instead of being sons of men; thus they have been devoured (as sons of men).]

53.6.6.en: St. Augustine often repeats that human wolves, when they devour human lambs and drink their blood, are changed from ravening wolves into gentle lambs, as happened with Saul of Tarsus. The wicked want to devour people and swallow them continually and without ceasing, as they eat bread daily, but as they eat them, some of them become sons of God by accepting the faith and enjoying baptism.

53.6.7.en: * This people who suffer from the wicked are devoured, this people who sigh and are in pain in the midst of the wicked; by this they are devoured.

53.7.0.en: When the Assyrians besieged Jerusalem they did not regard God but insulted Him, therefore He sent His angel to terrify them (2 Kgs 18).

53.7.1.en: He who does not call upon God for God Himself, but for temporal things, loses his joy in the gladness of salvation, and instead of peace fear comes upon him without any real cause except his deprivation of God, the source of peace.

53.7.2.en: * Some call, but they do not call upon him of whom it is said: "They have not called upon God" (Ps 53:4). They call, but they do not call upon God. You call what you love; you call what you are drawn to. So if you call upon God for this reason, that money may come to you; that you may receive an inheritance, or that a worldly rank may come to you, then you are calling upon these things which you desire to come to you, and you make God a helper to fulfill your lusts, not one who listens to your needs. What if you desire something evil? Would He not be merciful to you and not give it to you? And when He does not give it to you, God becomes nothing to you, and you say: How many times have I prayed, I have prayed often but He does not hear!

53.7.3.en: * It is fitting for us to call upon God, asking Him not for His temporal blessings, but seeking Him for His own person.

53.7.4.en: Do these not call upon God daily? They do not call upon God.

53.7.5.en: Take heed: if I am able to tell you, with the help of God Himself, that God must be worshipped freely (and not for the sake of good things), to be loved for His own sake freely, that is, loved with purity, not to give something, but to give Himself. He who wants God to be absent does not call upon God.

53.8.0.en: There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee.

53.8.1.en: Thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them [5].

53.8.2.en: "Thou hast put them to shame": if God allows the wicked to trouble His people and His believers, it is only for a time, but "He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision. Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure" (Ps 2:4-5).

53.8.3.en: And as the Lord said by the tongue of Isaiah concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria: "Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel. By thy messengers thou hast reproached the Lord, and hast said, With the multitude of my chariots I am come up to the height of the mountains... But I know thy abode, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy rage against me. Because thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears, therefore I will put my bridle in thy nose, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest" (2 Kgs 19:22-23, 27-28).

53.8.4.en: The Assyrians were at ease and in safety, and behold, terror fell upon them, and a hundred and eighty-five thousand soldiers perished among them (2 Kgs 19:35).

53.8.5.en: There was nothing to cause fear in the Lord Christ, who came to save the world, not to set up a temporal kingdom for Himself, and yet Herod was terrified and plotted to kill Him, and the Jewish leaders were terrified of Him and asked for His crucifixion.

53.8.6.en: St. Augustine sees that he who calls upon God does not fall into terror where there is nothing to cause real terror, for he says:

53.8.7.en: [Is there fear if a man loses riches? There is no fear, and yet men fear in this case. But if a man loses wisdom, then rather there is fear, and yet they do not fear...

53.8.8.en: You fear lest you return the money (which God gave you), and you want to lose salvation.]

53.8.9.en: "For God scattereth the bones of them that please men" [5]

53.8.10.en: He who does not call upon God fears where fear is not needed, because he cares to please his body and his lusts and also men, not God; but he who calls upon God fears no one but God, whom he seeks to please. The first, since he seeks to please men, is shattered, and loses his spiritual temple, and his bones are scattered.

53.8.11.en: * God scatters the bones of those who please men (Ps 53:5). By bones he does not mean here those of the body, for there is no example of a person whose bones are scattered in this way. Rather he means here the power of the mind and heart by which man can practice righteousness. These powers of the soul are the zeal that leads to earnest perseverance, spiritual maturity, patience and endurance. These traits God scatters in those who please men.

53.8.12.en: * He scatters the bones of those who please men... because the desire to please men is always the food of the accursed pride which God hates as men do, and it is the head and root of pride. He who falls victim to this passion desires honor and praise, and this is a thing God hates, for He hates the proud, but He receives the one who is humble in his thought, who does not seek glory, and shows him mercy.

53.9.0.en: * (The believer) must offer thanksgivings to God, the awesome, glorified, holy. And he must do nothing in a spirit of contention and vainglory (Phil 2:3), but for the glory of God and His good pleasure. "For God scattereth the bones of them that delight in evil" (Ps 53:5).

53.10.0.en: * The Apostle warns us, saying: "Let us not be conceited" (Gal 5:26). And the Lord rebukes the Pharisees, saying: "How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from the only God?!" (Jn 4:44) And of these also the blessed David speaks in warning: "The Lord hath scattered the bones of them that flatter men" (Ps 53:5).

53.10.1.en: * The soldier of Christ who desires to strive lawfully in this true spiritual battle must strive by every means to conquer this unsound, fickle, many-formed being, which, when it attacks us from every side like various manifold evils, we can escape by such a remedy as this: thinking of David's saying: "The Lord hath scattered the bones of them that flatter men" (Ps 53:5). At the beginning we must not allow ourselves to do anything out of conceit or to gain any vainglory. Likewise when we have begun something well, we must strive to strengthen it with the same care, lest the disease of vainglory creep in upon us and bring to nothing all the fruit of our labors.

53.11.0.en: * If you wish that no one should molest you, entreat God in secret and fast, and nothing will harm you. If the demons tell you to please men, do not accept, and remember what the Lord said: "Take heed that ye do not (your good deeds) before men, (but) in secret; and your Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward you openly" (Mt 6:1-4). And if Satan urges you to work to please men, look at the saying of the prophet: "God will scatter the bones of them that please men, He will put them to shame, for God despiseth them" [(Ps 53:5) cf. the Septuagint], and He does not listen to their prayer, but rather is wroth with them.

53.12.0.en: * "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven." If He had said only: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works," it would have seemed that He made the praise of men the aim, which is what the heretics seek, and those who ask for honors and those who rush after passing glory. It was said of these groups: "For if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ" (Gal 1:10), and the prophet says of those who pleased men: "Thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them," and "because God hath scattered the bones of them that please men" (Ps 53:5), and the Apostle says: "Because you are conceited" (Gal 5:26), as he says: "But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another" (Gal 6:4).

53.13.s.en: 4. The Church's rejoicing in spiritual freedom

53.13.0.en: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion.

53.14.0.en: When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad [6].

53.14.1.en: If ignorance causes the community (like a member) to lose its faith in God and its spiritual conduct so that it lives in corruption, not calling upon God for His own sake but seeking what is temporal, so that its bones are scattered and it loses its peace and even its very being, then salvation gives the Church freedom from the captivity of the devil, so she is filled with joy and rejoicing.

53.14.2.en: Father Anthimus of Jerusalem sees that the word "Israel" here is applied to every believer who beholds God with his mind, and the word "Jacob" is applied to everyone who wrestles with and pursues the enemy. It is as though the rejoicing Church is she who sees by faith God her Savior, and strives by the grace of God in her battle against the devil her enemy.

53.14.3.en: The expression "God bringeth back the captivity of his people" does not mean the Babylonian captivity, but the return of the people to their former glory after the enemy had humbled them for a time. This is what Holy Scripture meant when it spoke of the captivity of Job (Job 42:10), where the Lord restored him to his former glory before he entered into the trial.

53.14.4.en: Bringing back the captivity means return to glory and honor, as it came (Ezek 16:53; Zeph 2:7; Amos 9:14; Hos 6:11). If sin humbles man and brings the soul as into captivity, then repentance, or returning to God, grants release from captivity, and the enjoyment of rejoicing with honor and glory.

53.14.6.en: * On the cross, O Savior, You accepted the sufferings of love, and You travailed with us, Your Church and Your children!

53.14.7.en: You granted us to share Your sufferings, that we too may travail with new children, formed in Your likeness!

53.14.8.en: * You allowed the wicked to devour us like bread, so that they might be changed from sons of men into sons of God!

53.14.9.en: They devour us every day without ceasing, and You turn the affliction into a fruitful witness to the truth!

53.14.10.en: * The wicked do not call upon You, because they do not know You, so they are deprived of inner peace, and are terrified without cause!

53.14.11.en: But we see You, and we strive by Your grace, we are freed from the authority of the enemy, and we enjoy constant joy and heavenly rejoicing!
